content: The test image shows a soybean petiole/stem with dark reddish-brown to dark brown discoloration, while the attached leaves remain mostly green. This pattern — dark lesions on the petiole with green leaves — points toward Anthracnose or Diaporthe. Let me view reference images.

Based on my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Close-up of a soybean petiole/stem junction showing dark reddish-brown to nearly black, irregular discoloration along the petiole
- Leaves remain mostly green (not yellowed or necrotic)
- Dark blotchy lesions covering the petiole surface

**Reasoning:**
- **Anthracnose** matches best: "irregularly shaped red to dark brown blotches on stems and petioles" — the Anthracnose reference (bottom-left panel) shows an identical close-up of a dark brown, blotchy petiole with green leaves attached
- Diaporthe shows linear rows of black pycnidia specks on mature tan/brown stems — different pattern
- Brown Stem Rot affects internal stem tissue and causes interveinal chlorosis — doesn't match
- Phytophthora causes dark brown lesions extending from the soil line up the main stem — doesn't match
- Septoria, Bacterial Blight, SDS all affect leaf tissue primarily — don't match this petiole-focused lesion

The dark, irregular reddish-brown blotches specifically on the petiole while leaves stay green is the hallmark of Anthracnose petiole infection.
